records.subject: Need to encourage States and Union Territories to institute a transparent and inclusive mechanism for recognising meritorious students studying in Government schools.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Vijay Chintakayala:

I want to take this House back to 2003. A daughter stood outside a school while her father asked, ?What is the use of educating a girl?? Education was a burden, and educating a daughter, a shame. Children who could have led the world were left in the streets. Then our Honourable Prime Minister came and turned education into a celebration. Through schemes like Shala-Praveshotsav and Kanya-Kelavani, in Gujarat, encouraged our daughters to schools. Savitribai Phule said, ?Without education, a woman is like a banyan tree without roots or leaves.? Where once one in every three children dropped out, the dropout rate has reduced drastically. This is not politics. This is our conviction. Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya ji taught us that a nation?s progress is measured by the last person in the queue. That is Antyodaya. In 2026, India stands tall in AI, semiconductors and fighter jets built on Indian soil, from Kashmir to Kanyakumari. The challenge is no longer stigma. It is recognition. Our AP Government has demonstrated the power of recognition with full-page newspaper- advertisements featuring government-school Class X toppers, most of them being our daughters. The mother who never went to school could see her daughter on the front page. I urge the Government to launch schemes to in still pride among government school students and encourage every State and Union Territory to honour government-school toppers similarly. When the last child in the line rises, Bharat rises.

(ENDS)
